source: node .v1/helpers.js add-hypothesis '{"description":"convertCurrency in src/money.ts uses Math.floor(converted * 100) / 100 to round the converted amount to cents. Math.floor truncates toward zero, so a value like 92.349999... (the JS float result of 100 * 0.9235) becomes 92.34 instead of being rounded to 92.35. The same file defines roundToCents(value) = Math.round((value + Number.EPSILON) * 100) / 100 and uses it for add/subtract/multiply. convertCurrency is the only outlier. The function even carries an inline comment // BUG: truncates instead of rounding acknowledging the defect. Fix: replace Math.floor(...)/100 with roundToCents(converted).","evidence":["src/money.ts:convertCurrency returns Math.floor(converted * 100) / 100 instead of rounding","src/money.ts:inline comment `// BUG: truncates instead of rounding` directly above the buggy line","src/money.ts:roundToCents helper exists and is used by add/subtract/multiply/createMoney","tests/money.test.ts:convertCurrency precision test confirms the expected rounded behaviour for 999999.99 USD -> 923399.99 EUR (passes only because rate*amount is exactly representable; FP edge cases like 100*0.9235 -> 92.34999... exposed the bug)","repro: 100*0.9235 = 92.34999999999999 in JS, Math.floor-based code returns 92.34, roundToCents returns 92.35"],"confidence":0.99,"files":["src/money.ts","tests/money.test.ts"]}'
